intro: Bast Repository is a growing collection of participatory art projects that have taken place in Iran. Each project is presented as an entry written by the editorial team from the artist's own materials and a conversation with them, covering the setting, the process of participation, and the conditions the project worked within. Entries are accompanied by documentation, credits, and further sources, and some are joined later by a re-reading: an independent response from another artist, researcher, or cultural practitioner.

The repository does not set out to establish a definitive history. It gathers projects that took shape in different places and under different pressures, and each remains open to revision as new materials and readings arrive.

intro: The Bast Map provides two distinct points of entry to the repository: a chronological timeline and a geographic map. The timeline traces the temporal distribution of the projects gathered by the platform, while the map situates them across Iran.

Both visualisations show what the repository currently holds rather than a survey of the field; gaps in the timeline or on the map indicate where documentation has not yet been gathered, not where nothing took place.

intro: A re-reading (خوانش / Khanesh) is a response to a project held within the repository, approaching it from another position. This engagement may take the form of a critical interpretation, personal reflection, experiential account, or creative intervention, presented as a text, audio conversation, podcast, or other suitable medium.

Re-readings are initiated through invitations from the Bast editorial team, suggestions by the artists themselves, or proposals from external contributors seeking to engage with the archive. Each re-reading introduces new interpretive layers, extending the trajectory of the original work through an independent voice.
Not every project in the repository carries a re-reading. These texts accumulate gradually, and a project without one is simply a project still open to response.

The Bast Library is an evolving digital index of resources that approach participatory art from multiple perspectives. It brings together books, articles, interviews, and research texts from Iran and beyond, contributing to the theoretical, historical, and critical discourse surrounding the field.
The library also links to external digital archives, reading lists, and parallel research initiatives, continually expanding through the addition of new references.
Bast (بسط — from the Arabic root meaning to expand or to articulate) is a research and curatorial platform dedicated to the study, rethinking, and documentation of participatory art in Iran.

Through editorial and research-based work, Bast asks how participatory practices have responded to specific social, political, ecological, and institutional conditions, and what forms of collaboration, interaction, and creative agency they have proposed.

Participatory art encompasses practices that place participation, dialogue, collaboration, and collective action at the centre of the artistic process. Bast uses the term as an inclusive umbrella for a range of practices in which the work is shaped through the involvement of others, rather than as a fixed category. The terminology surrounding these practices is varied, and each term carries its own critical emphasis and evaluative framework; Bast therefore uses "participatory art" as a working term, open to different forms, contexts, and interpretations.

In Iran, many participatory initiatives have emerged, often in direct response to specific socio-political constraints, urgencies, and local conditions. They have taken many forms, including neighbourhood actions, workshops centred on conversation, long-term collaborations, and spaces for collective making. Many of these projects grew out of structural gaps, moments of crisis, and the absence of infrastructures for criticism and education, seeking instead to create alternative spaces for interaction and collective action. Bast is not limited to a single period or generation. Working with available documents, archival materials, and oral accounts, it also follows earlier projects and initiatives to trace a longer view of how participatory art has developed in Iran. Documenting and archiving these practices presents systemic challenges. The lack of centralised institutional resources, together with the fragmentation of existing materials, has contributed to the erasure of significant localised experiences from collective memory. The result is a substantial gap in the critical history of contemporary Iranian art, particularly with regard to participatory art practices.

Bast responds to this gap by operating as a counter-archive: a living archive of multiple voices in which documentation serves as a critical and creative methodology capable of generating knowledge, analysis, and the rearticulation of collective memory. This counter-archival approach intervenes in the documentation process, attempts to destabilise official narratives by focusing on human and personal accounts, and offers a space for alternative imaginaries to the established canon of art history. Within this framework, each archived project becomes a parallel opportunity for writing, creative interventions, and reactivation by artists, curators, researchers, and others.

Underlying this work is a shared awareness of the fragility of collective memory, of how easily particular histories disappear, and of the need to create spaces where marginalised voices can be heard. Our aim is to create a sustainable network of cultural practitioners who collectively preserve and re-read memory.

blocks.text: Making these examples accessible raises critical questions about the practice of participatory art, including where it has succeeded in creating meaningful interventions and where it has instead reproduced the very structures it sought to challenge; on whose terms participation was invited, and who was in a position to accept. It asks how to understand projects that were interrupted, left unfinished, or never documented, and whether such outcomes should be read as shortcomings of the work or as evidence of the conditions under which it was attempted. It also draws attention to the ethical considerations that arise when a participatory project is translated into institutional language for the purposes of evaluation or access.

Bast operates through three intersecting processes: collection, conversation, and re-reading. Each project is gathered, analysed through dialogue with its initiator(s), and subsequently opened to critical re-reading and creative mediation. This process is iterative rather than linear. Projects remain subject to reassessment, conversations evolve, interpretations stay open to contestation, and successive layers of analysis are incorporated.

items.label: Collection and selection:
items.text: The Bast team finds participatory art projects across a range of contexts through research, dialogues with practitioners, peer recommendations, and open calls. Projects are included not solely for their historical or aesthetic significance, but for their capacity to illuminate the social, institutional, and embodied dynamics that characterise participatory art in contemporary Iran.

items.label: Conversation with the artist:
items.text: Before any formal interpretation or re-reading takes place, the Bast team conducts in-depth conversations with the artist or project initiator(s). These conversations vary in format according to the nature of each project and its specific context, with the aim of uncovering the lived experience of the work. They address personal, social, and institutional frameworks, strategies for engaging participants, and the practical constraints encountered during the project's initiation, realisation, and aftermath.

items.label: Re-reading and creative mediation:
items.text: Every archived project serves as a point of departure for further engagement. Selected projects are accompanied by an invited re-reading by an artist, researcher, or cultural practitioner, offering an independent response to the original work. These re-readings are not bound to a single medium and may take the form of critical texts, personal reflections, experiential narratives, creative responses, dialogues, interactive web-based media, or other appropriate formats. Projects may also undergo creative mediation through reactivation, translation, or the structural reworking of the original project into new formats. Re-readings may be initiated by the original artist, the Bast team, or external practitioners seeking to engage with the archive.

items.label: Editorial ethics:
items.text: Archival entries are authored by the Bast team using materials provided by the artist, conversations with them, and available sources. An editorial note accompanies each entry, outlining its methodology and preparation. Details of rights of revision and withdrawal are set out in Intellectual Property and Copyright.

blocks.text: Bast is a collaborative platform that continues to grow through the participation of artists, researchers, writers, and cultural practitioners. There are two ways to contribute:

items.label: Suggest a project:
items.text: If you know of a participatory art project that could be included in the Bast Repository, whether it is your own work or that of another individual or group, you can share it with us by filling out the form below. The Bast team will review your submission and get in touch with you.

items.label: Propose a re-reading:
items.text: Submit a proposal in response to an existing project in the repository. Re-readings may take the form of critical interpretations, personal reflections, experiential narratives, or creative responses presented through text, audio, dialogue, or other media.

blocks.text: Bast is an independent, self-organised, non-profit research and curatorial platform, operating independently of any institution, commercial gallery, or funding body.

The privacy and security of project participants remain a primary editorial priority. The Bast team decides how archived materials are presented publicly, in consultation with the represented artists, collectives, and initiatives. Artists and collectives may revise, restrict, or withdraw their materials at any stage, before or after publication. Bast treats archiving as an editorial practice grounded in consent rather than a claim of record.

Materials published on Bast are available for non-profit research and educational purposes. Any reference to these materials must credit the creators of the material and name Bast as the research platform that published it, with a link to the relevant page on the website. Copyright for all participatory artworks remains with their original artists and creators; Bast claims no intellectual property rights in these works. Copyright for re-readings and supplementary texts remains with their respective authors and Bast. Documentation and data relating to artistic projects may not be used for commercial purposes or incorporated into external projects without the explicit consent of the artist(s) involved and the Bast team.

Materials originally published on Bast may be redistributed, provided they include full attribution and a link to bast.work. Materials that Bast republishes from secondary sources remain subject to the licensing terms established by their original publishers.
